name: Assessment Questions
purpose: A set of questions to assist stakeholders through their assessment (decision making) process.
whereUsed: The Assessment Questions is best used in the Problem Space during the Analysis Phase (2.5) to “Assess Readiness”. It’s also useful in the Solution Space to determine a solutions probability of success.
why: We will respond to key questions intentionally designed to uncover critical business priorities, requirements and criteria. This will avoid wasting time and resources for all stakeholders involved.
outcomes: Identification of early potential issues that will prevent the success of an initiative
Early-on and ongoing expectations for key stakeholders
Scope, time and resource expectations critical for success of an initiative or solution

spaces.heading: IF WE ARE IN THE “PROBLEM SPACE” WE NEED TO:
steps: Compare outcomes of the “Fast Path” vs. “The Gap”
Recognize the purpose for the questions is to increase the “odds of success” for an initiative or solution
Objectively review and refine answers to questions
List key takeaways (gaps, risks, actions, etc.)

spaces.heading: IF WE ARE IN THE “SOLUTION SPACE” WE NEED TO:
steps: Determine initiative or solution status (Fast Path, The Gap) and current “odds of success”
Confirm mutual interest to improve the “odds of success”
Objectively review and refine answers to questions
List key takeaways (gaps, risks, actions, etc.)
